messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Grand Piano with Bench Included
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rpkgteam,

I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to check in regarding the message I sent earlier about the Yamaha piano that belonged to my friend's late husband. It's a special piece with a lot of meaning, and she'd be so happy if it went to someone who truly appreciates music.

Please let me know if you're interested or know someone who might be.

I'd be grateful for any thoughts or connections you might have.

Many thanks,
Ms. Landes

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Looking Forward to Your Reply
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Looking Forward to Your Reply
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rpkgteam,

Just wanted to reach out again. I wanted to check in regarding the message I sent earlier about the Yamaha piano that belonged to my friend's late husband. This instrument holds profound sentimental value for her, and she'd love for it to find a new home with someone who will cherish it as much as her late husband did.

Please let me know if you're interested or know someone who might be.

Thank you for considering this, any help or advice is appreciated.

Sincerely,
Ms. Enedina

messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-gh
Version: 1.5.0-1
Severity: normal

-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----
Hash: SHA512

Hi,

while examining r-cran-gh for LTS, I found that the test suite actually doesn't
run any tests. In tests/testthat.R, there is a check for the value of the
NOT_CRAN environment variable. Because that one is not set, the test will
always return false and not run any tests.

After setting that variable, the testsuite will run, but fail at least one step
due to the test setup (tests/testthat/test-spelling.R), and skip other tests.
However, it would still improve the situation to actually run the remaining
tests.

Regards, Daniel

Package: r-cran-downlit
Version: 0.4.4-1
Severity: normal
X-Debbugs-Cc: edd at debian.org, edd at debian.org

When updating my (upstream) 'digest' package (aka 'r-cran-digest'), an
error in its reverse-dependency 'downlit' (aka 'r-cran-downlit') became
apparent. It made some assumptions about the 'URL' field in the 'DESCRIPTION'
file which leads a test failing under the updated 'digest'.

This has been fixed upstream (I had also sent a pull request), but Debian is
still at the affected version 0.4.4 so it is now blocking 'r-cran-digest' as
the autopkgtest fails, as expected.

If you upgrade to 0.4.5 all will be well.  Please do so at your convenience.

Hash: SHA512

[ Reason ]

The package is affected by CVE-2025-54956. The HTTP response is delivered in a
data structure that includes the Authorization header from the corresponding
HTTP request. This upload fixes this issue.

[ Impact ]

If not approved, users contionue to be vulnerable to CVE-2025-54956.

[ Tests ]

The testsuite runs successful. A few tests have been adjusted to the new
behavior. Their success is an indication that the changed code works and
nothing has been broken.

[ Risks ]

The main risks are regressions or breakages. But the test suite runs successful
and the code changes are not too complicated.

  [x] I reviewed all changes and I approve them
  [x] attach debdiff against the package in (old)stable
  [x] the issue is verified as fixed in unstable

[ Changes ]

The changes remove the request headers that were originally stored in the
response object. Instead, the sensitive information is passed explicitely.

n/a
